stories.headline: Norway’s new king swears oath of allegiance with daughter at his side

opening: Haakon VIII promises to uphold 1814 constitution but his queen misses ceremony because of post-surgery ‘complications’ King Haakon VIII swore an oath of allegiance before Norway’s parliament on Tuesday in the first major stage in the passing of the crown since the death of his father after 35 years on the throne.

Wearing a ceremonial uniform, Haakon, who became king when Harald V died on Friday, promised to uphold Norway’s 1814 constitution with his 22-year-old daughter, Crown Princess Ingrid Alexandra, by his side.

stories.title: Vanuatu tries to take island dispute with France to U.N.'s top court
stories.summary: The small Pacific Island state of Vanuatu is trying to bring a decades-old dispute with France over two uninhabited islands before the International Court of Justice, the United Nations' top court said on Tuesday. The ICJ, also known as the World Court, will not immediately accept the case because France has not agreed to so-called compulsory jurisdiction of the ICJ over its disputes with other states. Vanuatu's claim has been sent to Paris to see whether France agrees to let the court take it on, the ICJ said. "No action will be taken in the proceedings unless and until France consents to the Court’s jurisdiction in the case," the ICJ said in a press statement. The French government did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment on the matter. Vanuatu's case focuses on Matthew Island and Hunter Island, two volcanic islands in the South Pacific some 300 kilometres (190 miles) east of the French territory of New Caledonia and south-east of Vanuatu. While the islands are small and no one lives there, sovereignty over them also determines who controls the territorial waters surrounding them, which impacts fishing rights and exploitation of seabed resources. In 2025 France and Vanuatu agreed to new rounds of bilateral negotiations about the islands and the demarcation of the maritime boundaries between the territories after two earlier rounds of talks in 2018 and 2019. Earlier this year Vanuatu said the new talks had reached an impasse and it would take its case to an international court.

stories.title: Turkey, Russia enjoy unprecedented level of bilateral relations development — Erdogan
stories.summary: The significance of Russian tourists for Turkey is very great and multifaceted, the Turkish president added
article_sentences: BISHKEK, September 1.
Relations between Russia and Turkey are currently at the highest possible level, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said on Tuesday.
"Turkish-Russian relations are currently at a much higher level than at any other point in history," Erdogan said at his meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek.
"The significance of Russian tourists for Turkey is very great and multifaceted.
Russian tourists form today one of the most important components of the tourist flow to Antalya," the Turkish president continued.
Erdogan added that, "in addition to this, the two countries have strong partnership relations in agriculture and energy," as well as in other spheres.

stories.title: Russia’s governing hockey body appeals IIHF’s ban on national teams with CAS
stories.summary: On July 30, the IIHF announced a decision to extend Russia’s suspension from international tournaments until 2027
article_sentences: MOSCOW, September 1.

The Russian Ice Hockey Federation (RHF) has filed an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) in Lausanne against the decision of the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) to extend the suspension of Russian national teams, the RHF press office announced in a statement on Tuesday.
"The Russian Ice Hockey Federation appealed the decisions of the International Ice Hockey Federation to the Court of Arbitration for Sport in Lausanne," the statement reads.
On July 30, the IIHF announced a decision to extend Russia’s suspension from international tournaments until 2027.

According to the IIHF statement in July: "Following the IIHF Disciplinary Board Decision, the IIHF Council re-analyzed the Russian Ice Hockey Federation’s request that it be permitted to enter a Russian Team in each of the following IIHF Championships: IIHF Men’s World Championship 2027; IIHF Women’s World Championship 2027; IIHF World Junior Championship 2027; IIHF U18 Men’s World Championship 202; and IIHF U18 Women’s World Championship 2027.".
